transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-18 | Time: 09:00 PT | Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Samira Roy (Redwood SE), Carlos Ortega (Nebulus Head of Partnerships), Priya Nair (Nebulus Cloud SA), Evan Lu (Nebulus CEO)

Summary: quick partner intro + discovery; high-level GTM interest + technical integration questions.
Topics: partnership models (resell vs. integrated Dedicated), private deployment options, security/compliance, benchmarks and performance targets, timelines.

Transcript:
00:00 Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, im Jordan kim, AE at Redwood, super excited to meet the Nebulus team. can you quick intro yourselves?
00:13 Carlos: yeah hey, carlos here, head of partnerships at Nebulus, we build GPU appliances and private cloud stacks, we've been talking to a few inference platforms, interested in how Redwood might fit.
00:28 Priya: hi priya, lead cloud solutions, i'll be technical point, mainly around network/connectivity and interconnects.
00:36 Evan: evan here, CEO, hey all.
00:40 Jordan: awesome, quick agenda — intro to redwood, partnership models we do, then samira will cover technical fit and then open q&a. sound good?
00:52 Samira: yep i'll jump in with the runtime details, trickier bits — kv cache, batching, quantization profiles, kernel selection, things that matter for your hw.
01:05 Jordan: high level — redwood is a developer-first inference platform for hosted, dedicated and private deployments. for partners we'd typically explore either a channel resell where Nebulus sells Redwood Dedicated pre-bundled on your racks, or a closer integration so Redwood can target workloads to Nebulus capacity via our smart routing.
01:30 Carlos: yeah that's what we're curious about — do you need us to run your control plane, or can we keep our customers on our control plane? what's the options?
01:38 Samira: good q. we have a private deployment option — customers can run a customer-managed control plane (VPC/on-prem) while we still provide the orchestration and updates. alternately we can run a private control plane in a joint tenancy model. both are possible; the big differences are around audit logs, SSO integration, and where KMS keys live.
02:02 Priya: ok, for some of our telco customers they require KMS in their HSM and no external key egress. can you support that?
02:10 Samira: yes — we've done HSM integrations; we expose KMS integration points and can operate without keys leaving the customer boundary. small note — that increases onboarding time and we usually treat it as an enterprise private deployment.
02:24 Evan: from GTM perspective, we like resell but also co-sell where Nebulus hardware + Redwood Dedicated is a recommended stack for ML inference customers. how do you handle pricing and SLAs for dedicated?
02:38 Jordan: dedicated is reserved capacity contracts — monthly/annual commits, SLA-backed latency and uptime targets. we'd work with sales to define margin split for partners; we can share a partner deck after this call.
02:52 Carlos: great. on the tech side, priya will want to know about model compatibility — HF models, Llama variants, and custom models. do you do quantization? any kernel selection issues for our accelerators?
03:06 Samira: we support a wide model catalog; we compile kernels per architecture and we have quantization profiles (8-bit, int4-ish) that we test. depends on your substrate — if you provide a metal layer similar to CUDA or ROCm, we can optimize. we do continuous batching and prefix/KV caching to improve unit economics.
03:28 Priya: what about sequence lengths and memory for KV cache? some of our customers do long-context LLMs.
03:36 Samira: kv cache is managed — we tune caching behavior by workload. long sequences affect kernel selection and scheduling; we may suggest sharded KV caches or specific batching policies to keep latency SLOs.
03:50 Jordan: also, we offer smart routing — route by cost/latency/region. Nebulus could be a cost-preferent target in our routing policies if we validate performance.
04:03 Carlos: curious about telemetry — do you expose per-token cost/latency, traces? our ops team wants telemetry to integrate into their dashboards.
04:12 Samira: yes — Redwood Console exposes token-level cost, per-route dashboards, traces, and we can push metrics to your Prom/Datadog endpoints. logs can be configured to avoid PII and adhere to customer retention policies.
04:28 Priya: security — SOC 2, ISO? we need evidence to show to customers.
04:33 Jordan: we're SOC 2 compliant — we'll share certs and security pack. for private deployments we support SAML SSO and RBAC, and we can integrate with customer KMS.
04:44 Priya: perfect. also curious about network topology — do you need a direct connect / peering to reach your control plane?
04:51 Samira: for hosted we do secure peering; for private deployments we typically run inside the customer's VPC with private endpoints. depends on latency requirements: if you want sub-10ms internal p50 we'd recommend colocated control plane or on-prem option.
05:12 Evan: benchmark question — what do you need from us to validate Nebulus hardware as a target for Redwood?
05:19 Samira: we'd want a benchmark harness and a sample model (or a set of models) and a representative workload. we'd run P50/P95 latency and throughput with typical sequence length distributions. ideally access to a test cluster or a VM with your images.
05:33 Carlos: ok we'll prepare a short benchmark spreadsheet and share configs.
05:38 Jordan: on the commercial side — if Nebulus resells Redwood Dedicated, we usually have partner pricing and referral credits. we can explore a co-sell motion once we have a technical validation.
05:50 Priya: one more — multi-tenancy. can you do strict tenant isolation on dedicated pools? some of our customers require no noisy neighbors.
05:58 Samira: yes — Dedicated offers dedicated GPU pools per customer plus configurable autoscaling and burst policies. isolation is physical or cgroup-based depending on the deployment.
06:12 Jordan: i'm going to tee up an initial partner contract template later, but first let's validate technical fit.
06:18 Carlos: good. any competitors you see in this space? we mentioned PicoCloud and Orion, any nuance?
06:25 Samira: those two are common; PicoCloud focuses on easy on-demand endpoints, Orion on hardware + software stacks. Redwood differentiator: unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private and batching/cost controls.
06:40 Evan: timeline — if we like the tech, could we be ready for a joint pilot in 8-12 weeks?
06:47 Samira: technically yes, assuming we get cluster access and security signoff. to meet that timeline we'd prioritize the benchmark and the private deployment checklist.
06:56 Jordan: ok let's recap next steps — i'll send the partner one-pager, pricing deck and partner program overview; samira will schedule a tech deep-dive and benchmark run; nebulus will share infra specs and a point of contact.
07:12 Carlos: sounds good. thanks everyone.

(Transcription notes: occasional mis-hearings - 'KV cash' for KV cache, 'pico cloud' sometimes spelled 'peek-o cloud', named entities slightly off. occasional crosstalk on timeline items.)
